# Compatibility: features and run profiles

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_compatibility_doc.py from
     openadapt_flow/compatibility.py. Edit those, not this file. -->

Each feature either works under a run profile or is refused with a
named reason. Nothing falls back silently. When a run takes the slower or
narrower path, it records why: an API step's `api_fallback`, a
pipelined read-back's `inline_reason`, or the command's refusal before
anything runs. `tests/test_compatibility_matrix.py` checks every cell
against the runtime, and fails when a cell that should work falls back
or a refusal gives another reason.

## The widest combination today

A Regulated, durable, governed run with per-item approval, on parallel
workers, using the API step for an admitted save, is the combination
where the most work together: each worker's item sends one request a
person approved, checks it with the system-of-record read-back, and
reads `VERIFIED`. In that run the read-back runs inline (durable), and
self-repair runs through the Python API under the Standard contract.
Under a signed qualification admission (what `openadapt-flow run`
requires for Standard and Regulated actuation) the API step and
self-repair are still refused, each with its reason below.

## Profiles

- **Default (gated).** `openadapt-flow run` with no `--profile`: a run authorization from the run gate, and per-item approval (`each_item`), the default approval mode.
- **Durable.** `--durable`: a checkpoint after every verified step, and pause and resume from the last one.
- **Governed.** The Standard or Regulated profile contract with a run authorization from the run gate: durable, an identity check on every save, and a record check that reads the system of record. This is how the Python API and the tutorial run it.
- **Pinned.** `--pin-digest`: the run refuses any bundle but the one with that sealed content digest.
- **Qualified.** A signed production qualification admission (`--qualification-authority-file`), which `openadapt-flow run` requires for Standard and Regulated actuation.
- **Managed.** A Cloud-dispatched run (`--managed-dispatch-file`), whose run authorization comes from Cloud.

## Features

- **API step** ([API_TIER.md](API_TIER.md)). An admitted save compiled from network capture, run as one request in place of its GUI steps.
- **Pipelined read-back** ([THROUGHPUT.md](THROUGHPUT.md)). `--readback-window`: an item's record check runs while the next item starts.
- **Self-repair** ([SELF_REPAIR.md](SELF_REPAIR.md)). `--self-repair`: an agent proposes a fix for a halt on a changed screen; probes and a person's approval decide it.
- **Standard changes** ([SELF_REPAIR.md](SELF_REPAIR.md#standard-changes-repairs-without-a-person)). Self-repair fixes of a class a person approved in advance, in a signed repair policy.
- **Parallel workers** ([THROUGHPUT.md](THROUGHPUT.md)). `--workers N`: worklist items on several signed-in sessions at once.
- **Multi-surface** ([MULTI_SURFACE.md](MULTI_SURFACE.md)). One program across several windows, tabs or apps.

## At a glance

| Feature | Default (gated) | Durable | Governed | Pinned | Qualified | Managed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API step | Works | Works | Works | Works | Refused | Works |
| Pipelined read-back | Works | Refused | Refused | Works | Refused | Refused |
| Self-repair | Works | Works | Works | Works | Refused | Refused |
| Standard changes | Works | Works | Works | Works | Refused | Refused |
| Parallel workers | Works | Works | Works | Works | Works | Refused |
| Multi-surface | Works | Works | Works | Works | Works | Works |

Every refusal names its reason (below), and a run or command that
refuses says it in those words.

## Features by profile

### API step

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works: the person approves the exact request |
| Durable | Works: a save that may have landed is never resent |
| Governed | Works: needs `api admit --identity` |
| Pinned | Works: the pin is checked before the run |
| Qualified | Refused: a production qualification admission doesn't cover API steps yet, so the qualified GUI path runs |
| Managed | Works: Cloud's authorization names the API step, and each send still needs Cloud's delivery permit |

### Pipelined read-back

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works: GUI and API saves |
| Durable | Refused: durable runs verify inline (the record check runs before the next item) |
| Governed | Refused: durable runs verify inline (Standard and Regulated are durable) |
| Pinned | Works: when the run isn't durable |
| Qualified | Refused: durable runs verify inline (Standard and Regulated are durable) |
| Managed | Refused: --workers and --readback-window apply to local runs, not a managed dispatch or a qualification case |

### Self-repair

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works |
| Durable | Works: self-repair always runs durable |
| Governed | Works: Standard contract through the Python API |
| Pinned | Works: needs repair.requalify: the fix is re-qualified on a test copy and re-admitted with signed lineage, and the pin accepts that new version |
| Qualified | Refused: a production qualification admission is signed by the qualification authority, so a repaired bundle waits for that authority's signature |
| Managed | Refused: a managed dispatch is Cloud's authorization for one bundle, so a repaired bundle runs only on a new dispatch from Cloud |

### Standard changes

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works: needs a signed repair policy |
| Durable | Works: needs a signed repair policy |
| Governed | Works: needs a signed repair policy |
| Pinned | Works: needs repair.requalify, as self-repair |
| Qualified | Refused: a production qualification admission is signed by the qualification authority, so a repaired bundle waits for that authority's signature |
| Managed | Refused: a managed dispatch is Cloud's authorization for one bundle, so a repaired bundle runs only on a new dispatch from Cloud |

### Parallel workers

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works |
| Durable | Works: each item has its own durable run |
| Governed | Works: each item gets its own single-use authorization |
| Pinned | Works |
| Qualified | Works: the admission is checked for every item |
| Managed | Refused: --workers and --readback-window apply to local runs, not a managed dispatch or a qualification case |

### Multi-surface

| Profile | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (gated) | Works: an API step inside it runs on the GUI (below) |
| Durable | Works: resume re-binds each surface by identity |
| Governed | Works |
| Pinned | Works |
| Qualified | Works: one environment boundary per surface |
| Managed | Works: every backend surface must be bound |

## The API step with the other features

| With | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Parallel workers | Works: each item runs its own API step |
| Pipelined read-back | Works: when the run isn't durable |
| Self-repair | Refused: self-repair's probes and resumed run exercise the repaired GUI step, and the person approved that step, so its API step doesn't run (the first, ordinary run can use the API step) |
| Standard changes | Refused: self-repair's probes and resumed run exercise the repaired GUI step, and the person approved that step, so its API step doesn't run (the repaired bundle's test-record run is GUI-only too) |
| Multi-surface | Refused: a run across several windows or tabs uses the GUI steps |
